geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the dominant bar mutation from a simple clip into a void-producing gesture to better support neighborhood public space.
Increase the carved court size enough to be legible in all views while preserving the primary bar.
Open the dominant void toward the access edge to create a readable ground threshold.

graph_edits.rationale: Strengthen the street-facing public space by converting the primary volume into a court-producing mass instead of a mostly sealed bar.
Create a more legible, usable void without over-dissolving the dominant mass.
Align the void opening with the verified access side so the frontage becomes a public threshold.
Retarget the terrace/bridge logic to the access side so the public edge reads as an active entry seam.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent bar-derived mass across all four views, so it avoids the one-view-only failure and does not show obvious inter-view collisions. The dominant gesture is legible: a long primary bar with a localized lift/void condition and a small stepped/angled end response. However, the public-space figure is still weak; the blue frontage is met mostly by a sealed edge rather than a clearly carved, welcoming ground seam, so the access relationship is only partially resolved. Program-wise, the mass plausibly supports neighborhood living as a compact mixed-use street building, but it remains somewhat generic and boxy compared with the best references, lacking a stronger articulated court/terrace threshold. Sectionally it is acceptable but not especially expressive of active ground or public sequence.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact community mass with a clear central void and a softened upper edge can support neighborhood-scale public program.
Terraced/clustered low-rise masses around a shared court can create legible public space while keeping the composition coherent.
A long low bar paired with a central courtyard and strong horizontal spread is relevant to active-ground neighborhood program.
Ribbon-like continuity, layered sections, and a public terrace/court figure translate well to a neighborhood-living massing brief.
Interlocking volumes around a courtyard with some lifted ground condition can support mixed-use neighborhood hierarchy.

warnings: The road frontage is visible but not strongly articulated as an entry court or porous ground threshold.
The form is coherent but still close to a generic extruded bar; it could benefit from a clearer carved void or notch toward the access edge.
Upper massing is calm, but the section does not yet strongly advertise the public-program relationship.
